# VerifyOps: progress and history

Spec: `text_to_pdf_Imagetotext.pdf` (kept outside this repo). Repo: `C:\dev\verifyops` (outside OneDrive on purpose: sync can corrupt SQLite files).
Model used for every result in this repo: `mistral/ministral-14b-latest` through LiteLLM, on Mistral's free plan.
**All evaluation numbers live in `evals/RESULTS.md` (S1-S5, the frozen set) and `evals/RESULTS_PHASE7.md` (the new tasks). Both are generated by code from stored run records; nothing in this file repeats them, so they cannot drift apart.**

## What exists (details: `docs/DECISIONS_LOG.md`, 108 entries)

- **Mock company** (`apps/company/`): vendor portal (amount and due date only inside invoice PDFs), ERP with web forms and a JSON API, token-protected admin, faults `DATE_TRAP`, `SAVE_BROKEN`, `BUTTON_RENAME`, `DUPLICATE_VENDOR` (off by default), deterministic seed. `SESSION_EXPIRY` (P2) is not built.
- **Auditor** (`auditor/`, plain Python, no model, no company words): own read-only SQLite connection, schema-checked SQL, before/after row-hash snapshots, six assertion kinds, a validator that forces coverage of what the handbook requires and independent sources for those values, declaration-time checks (expected values must resolve now, undeclared changes are refused with the exact fix), `no_other_changes`, a feedback ladder.
- **Policy gate** (`agent/gate.py`): host allow-list, deny rules on every method including GET, writes must map to a named action, fail-closed on unreadable input, approvals that are action-keyed, single-use and described by the gate.
- **Tools and detectors**: real Chromium with every request gated (redirect guard, 204 for refused navigations), `http_request`, `read_document`, `note`, `ask_human`; detectors `tool_error`, `timeout`, `noop`, `unexpected_page`, `repeat` (including identical writes sent twice).
- **The loop** (`agent/loop.py`): state, not transcript; one tool call per step with a reason; budgets 60 steps / 600 s / $1 per run; `finish(done)` only with validated assertions and a passing audit; a final report whose outcome, evidence and changes are written by code.
- **Handbook** (`company_pack/`): four procedures (rules, "where the truth is", definition of done; no click paths and no real values), policy, connectors, the audit map.
- **Evals** (`evals/`): scenarios S1-S5, S6, S7, S10; fresh data copy and app process per run; an independent ground-truth check (not the auditor); metrics including "auditor false pass"; `RESULTS.md` generated from stored records.
- **Proof of generalization** (`scripts/prove_generalization.py`): hashes of `agent/` and `auditor/` at the freeze.
- **Web console** (`apps/console/`): `python -m apps.console.main`, then http://127.0.0.1:8500. Runs the real agent in a thread, shows phases, plan, every step with its reason, the gate, the auditor's checks beside the agent's own claim, and the company's tables live; a person answers approvals and questions in the browser; also shows the generated results and the freeze proof.
- **Tests**: 812 (about 3 to 4 minutes) after phase 10. The 761-test run and the clean-clone install were done on the earlier commit `8433174`; the clean clone was not repeated after phase 10.

## How the real model changed the code

The architecture was written and tested with a scripted fake model; the first real runs (2026-10-09) showed what a real, small model does. Every item below was a defect found by a real run, fixed generically (no task words in `agent/` or `auditor/`; a test enforces that), and logged in `docs/DECISIONS_LOG.md`:

- **Provider limits.** The free Gemini key allows 20 calls per day per model (a run needs about 25); Mistral's Medium and Small models answered HTTP 429 with a request limit of 0 on this key, although the Limits page showed 20,000 tokens per minute; `ministral-14b-latest` worked (30 requests and 937,500 tokens per minute) and accepted all tool definitions. Schemas were made conservative because Gemini accepts only a small JSON Schema subset; LiteLLM's own retries needed an optional package, so the client has its own retry loop.
- **Assertion writing was the hard part for a 14B model.** Fixes: regex examples in single quotes (YAML rejected `\s` in double quotes 22 times in a row), a "Verification so far" section in the state (the model re-declared accepted assertions nine times because the acceptance scrolled out of the 3-step window), declaration-time lookup of expected values, declaration-time refusal of an undeclared added row with the exact fix, and a handbook section naming the independent sources.
- **Loop bugs the fake model could not show:** a closed keyboard crashed `ask_human`; a deadlock when the human was unavailable (finish was refused); the retry budget counted scattered mistakes instead of consecutive ones; the model forgot its own write (now listed from the gate's log); an identical write sent twice was not noticed (now a `repeat`).
- **Prompt and handbook wording** for over-asking, over-selecting rules, comparing DD/MM/YYYY dates by day number alone, wrong local document paths, and `blocked` versus `needs_human`.
- **Defaults:** time budget 300 s -> 600 s and step budget 40 -> 60, because normal runs on this model need 150-330 s and up to about 50 steps when they must notice and repair a wrong value.

## Things I got wrong, and how they were handled

- **Example values in the handbook (about 08:27 to 09:40 on 2026-10-09).** I briefly wrote real values (an invoice number, an amount, a date) as examples in the handbook; the model copied them into a different vendor's bill, and the agent could pass by copying the handbook instead of reading the document. Every run from that period is excluded from the evidence (including the first "success" sample, which I deleted). The text now describes line labels and tables only, and `tests/test_handbook_has_no_answers.py` fails if any seed value appears in the pack. The evaluation was run afterwards on clean text.
- **Development runs overlap scenario S1.** 14 single development runs and 5 pilot batches (26 runs, so about 40 runs in all) used the same tasks as S1-S5, with fixes between them (decisions #77-#97). Evaluation numbers are therefore not independent of that tuning, S3 in particular (decision #92). The new tasks (S6, S7, S10) were not run before the freeze.
- **T2-T4 handbook files and their scenarios were written before the freeze** but never run before it; they were in the handbook catalogue during every S1-S5 run (which also tests that extra rules do not confuse the agent). So `prove_generalization` shows the agent code unchanged and, as data changes since the freeze, only the S6 handbook fix (`company_pack/sops/invoice_revision_update.md`) and a corrected out-of-date comment in `evals/scenarios.yaml` (no scenario changed): the honest claim is "the same frozen code ran four tasks", not "data was added after the freeze".

## Known gaps (honest list)

See `docs/LIMITATIONS_AND_FUTURE.md` for the full list with reasoning. In short: one small model on a free plan; the agent writes its own assertions and a handbook note makes that feasible; the auditor checks the record against the source the agent cites, so a wrong choice of source (the wrong "latest" invoice) is only visible to the harness's independent ground-truth check; the model does not reliably ask when two vendors have similar names; three runs per scenario is a small sample; humans are scripted in the evals; Windows only.

## Provider research (2026-10-09, kept for the record)

What a run needs: about 25 model calls and 150,000-250,000 tokens. Groq (Developer plan: 8,000 tokens per minute): not viable. Cerebras (1 million tokens per day but needs a verified payment method). OpenRouter free models (50 per day without credits): not viable. GitHub Models: retired. Cohere trial key (1,000 calls per month): about 40 runs. NVIDIA NIM: reported free, not tried. Mistral free plan: used (limits above). Gemini free key: 20 calls per day per model, used for the first partial run only (`runs/` evidence not kept).

## Phase 10: why the freeze tag moved, and what changed

**The finding.** Reading the stored runs showed that the agent never asked a human when two records looked alike: in all 6 stored runs with the DUPLICATE_VENDOR fault it saw both look-alike vendors on the vendor list, wrote, and asked nothing; across the 77 stored `run.json` files no clarification question was ever answered. The only code that forced a question read the request text once, before any page was seen, and the prompt had told the model to leave that list empty (decisions #85, #52). The gate also let a request through when a policy field such as the amount was missing, and it only stood safe because the mock ERP rejected those requests itself. Nothing in the code answered for the human: scripted, console and web humans have no default answer (checked, with real runs of the approve and deny paths).

**What changed (decisions #103-#108).**
- `agent/gate.py`, `agent/policy.py`, `agent/connectors.py`, new `agent/similar.py`: a missing or unreadable policy field means a human must approve (reason logged); a write that points at a record with a look-alike is blocked until a human has answered a question asked after the block. Which field names the record, where the candidates are listed and which words to ignore are data in `company_pack/connectors/erp.yaml`.
- `agent/toolbox.py`, `agent/loop.py`: the human sees what the gate found; an empty reply is not an answer; if no human can answer, code ends the run as `needs_human` and records why.
- `apps/console/static/index.html`, `scripts/render_run.py`: show the new gate decision.
- The suite grew from 761 to 812 tests, and the old tests that encoded the previous behaviour (a missing amount allowed, an unreadable amount denied, the agent expected to stop by itself) were rewritten on purpose, not loosened. Full suite: 812 passed.

**Why the tag moved.** `agent/` and `auditor/` changed, so the old claim "this code is byte-identical to the evaluated freeze" no longer holds for the new code. Editing the old tag would have hidden that. Instead the new code is tagged `agent-frozen-v2` with its own hash manifest (`evals/frozen_manifest.json`); the first manifest is kept as `evals/frozen_manifest_v1.json`, and the first results as `evals/RESULTS_before_fix.md`, generated from the stored batch. Everything measured on the first freeze (S3-advisory, S4, S6, S7, S10 and the S1 to S5 sweep) belongs to the first freeze; only S1, S2, S3, S5-approve and S5-deny were re-run on the second. `scripts/prove_generalization.py` still prints its `git diff` against the tag `agent-frozen` (the first freeze).

**Not fixed, on purpose.** The agent is still allowed to choose the wrong record when the names do not look alike (S5-approve's older invoice, S6's original document): that is the auditor's blind spot, listed in the README. A test that failed once under full-suite load (`test_the_agents_log_writes_and_the_consoles_reads_never_overlap`, passed 5 of 5 alone and in the 812-test run) was not investigated.
